specification.title: The connection is terminated inside a nested scope that then fails
steps: Start the outer transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of one connection.
Write the marker `outer`, and make sure the write was sent.
Start a nested scope with the framework's nested-transaction (savepoint) API. Write the marker `inner` in it, and make sure the write was sent.
Checkpoint `inner-after-write`: report the backend PID. The runner sees the savepoint's subtransaction lock. The runner then terminates the backend, and waits until it has gone.
Wait settle_ms, then raise an application error in the nested scope; its ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fails on the closed connection.
The outer scope catches the nested scope's error.
Checkpoint `after-outer`, after the outer transaction's API has returned: report the same backend PID. The runner records whether that session is still inside a transaction.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If the API reports that the outer transaction committed, PostgreSQL committed it, with the outer scope's writes and none of the failed nested scope's writes.
When the outer transaction's API has returned, the connection that ran it is no longer inside a transaction.

execution.description: Database.BeginTransactionAsync, CommitAsync, and RollbackAsync. Marker inserts use Database.ExecuteSqlAsync. The native TX-01A violation is SaveChangesAsync, which EF Core wraps in a savepoint. Nested scopes use CreateSavepointAsync. Pooling is false. EnableRetryOnFailure is not called. The provider's default execution strategy is left in place.

configuration.writes: Database.ExecuteSqlAsync for markers; SaveChangesAsync for the native TX-01A unique violation
configuration.savepoints: CreateSavepointAsync, RollbackToSavepointAsync, ReleaseSavepointAsync; SaveChangesAsync may create its own savepoint
configuration.execution_strategy: the provider default; EnableRetryOnFailure is not called

execution.form: The outer transaction is BeginTransactionAsync. The nested scope is CreateSavepointAsync, RollbackToSavepointAsync, and ReleaseSavepointAsync. A second BeginTransactionAsync is not used.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: pg_terminate_backend(pid), run by the runner from its own connection.
fault.injection_point: Inside the nested scope, after its write, before the framework's savepoint rollback.
fault.preconditions: The PID the adapter reports belongs to the case's database.
fault.expected_server: The backend exits, and the whole transaction is rolled back.
fault.expected_client: Connection errors for the savepoint rollback and for anything after it.

knowledge: The framework sees its connection fail during the savepoint rollback.

api_outcome.contract: EF Core 10 IDbContextTransaction.CommitAsync commits the transaction begun by Database.BeginTransactionAsync. The EF Core transaction API does not return a PostgreSQL command tag. A return from CommitAsync is reported as committed. A throw from CommitAsync is reported as failed. A throw from the body followed by RollbackAsync returning is reported as rolled_back. A throw from RollbackAsync is reported as failed. Marker inserts use Database.ExecuteSqlAsync. SaveChangesAsync inside an explicit transaction inserts the row under a savepoint and releases it; the row xmin is then that subtransaction, while pg_current_xact_id() is the top-level id, and the harness does not attribute that xmin to a top-level write. The native TX-01A violation is still SaveChangesAsync of a Uniq entity. The execute-sql mode uses ExecuteSqlAsync for that violation. A nested scope is CreateSavepointAsync, RollbackToSavepointAsync, and ReleaseSavepointAsync. EF Core creates its own savepoint around SaveChangesAsync when a user transaction is already active and the transaction reports SupportsSavepoints. This adapter does not disable that savepoint and does not read Npgsql protocol messages.

error.message: application error: the nested scope fails

rollback_error.message: 57P01: terminating connection due to administrator command

evaluation.reason: TX-02.1 held: the API reported: failed; xid 7570 rolled back at report time (`after-outer`); outer visible: false; inner (failed scope) visible: false; TX-02.2 held: the session after the outer API returned: closed

preconditions.description: the write of marker "outer" had reached PostgreSQL at `outer-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the write of marker "inner" had reached PostgreSQL at `inner-after-write` (a subtransaction lock, in pg_locks)
the runner terminated the backend at `inner-after-write`, and it had gone before the adapter resumed
the nested scope's error reached the outer scope, which handled it
the runner observed the transaction's session after the outer API returned

invariants.statement: If the API reports that the outer transaction committed, PostgreSQL committed it, with the outer scope's writes and none of the failed nested scope's writes.
invariants.detail: the API reported: failed; xid 7570 rolled back at report time (`after-outer`); outer visible: false; inner (failed scope) visible: false

invariants.statement: When the outer transaction's API has returned, the connection that ran it is no longer inside a transaction.
invariants.detail: the session after the outer API returned: closed

controls.detail: CTL-01.commit and CTL-01.rollback PASSed for efcore (native)

case_controls.detail: pg-control (correct) expected PASS, got PASS, pg-control (unsafe) expected PASS, got PASS
